newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil gov't edges closer to re-election majority.
newsitem.headline: Brazil gov't edges closer to re-election majority.

text.p: The Brazilian government is making progress towards securing the three-fifths majorities it needs in the Chamber of Deputies for approval of re-election, a government source in Congress said.

The government needs two three-fifths majorities, each equivalent to 308 votes, for approval of a constitutional amendment which would allow re-election for a second term for presidents, state governors and mayors. "From what I hear, there's at least 275 deputies on the government's side," said the source, adding that some estimates put the government only 15 votes short of its 308 target.

The source, who asked not to be identified, said the government would seek the support of at least 340 deputies before putting re-election to a vote on the floor of the lower house. He also said the government would probably call an extraordinary session of Congress, beginning January 6 or 7, allowing for a vote in a lower house panel on the amendment around January 8.
The bill would then be put to a first vote on the floor of the Chamber of Deputies, ideally on January 15, with a second vote taking place before the end of the month, the source said.
The government was confident the amendment would be approved without difficulty in the panel but it faced a rougher ride on the volatile floor of the lower house, he said.

The government hoped the re-election amendment would clear the lower house before Dep. Luiz Eduardo Magalhaes, the president of the Chamber of Deputies and a staunch defender of the government's reforms, stood down on February 2, he said.
